paper_title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of $432$ strictly paired test cases across $48$ executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a $3 \times 3$ factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. Extensive evaluations across $12$ representative models reveal that: (I) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (II) richer draft scaffolding anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (III) conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage (up to $64\%$), exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer lay a foundation for bridging programmatic 4D simulation with video generation, advancing physically grounded generative rendering.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Video generation has achieved remarkable progress in visual realism and temporal coherence, yet generating complex, controllable dynamic scenes remains challenging (Wan et al., 2025; Agarwal et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026a; HaCohen et al., 2024). Since end-to-end models must implicitly infer 4D world evolution from brief text while simultaneously generating pixels, high visual quality often comes at the expense of physical and spatiotemporal reliability. Recently, advances in multimodal coding agents have enabled an alternative paradigm that decouples world construction from visual generation (Li et al., 2026b; Wang et al., 2026a; Liang et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026). By programmatically controlling engines such as Blender (Blender Online Community, 2026) or MuJoCo (Todorov et al., 2012), coding agents can explicitly specify scene layouts, object trajectories, and physical interactions as executable simulation drafts, leaving video generation models to transform these low-fidelity drafts into photorealistic videos. This emerging division of labor explores repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers, raising fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? We thus argue that reliable generative renderer hinges on fulfilling two complementary objectives: ❶ world preservation, which demands faithfully retaining the scene geometry, object dynamics, event timing, and camera motion prescribed by the draft without rewriting the underlying world; and ❷ visual realization, which requires accurately generating text-specified target attributes (e.g., color, material) while persistently binding them to the corresponding 4D entities across motion, occlusion, and viewpoint changes. Formally, generative rendering operates as conditional video-to-video (V2V) transformation guided by structural draft and target text prompt, yet existing benchmarks only partially address its requirements. Early V2V benchmarks (Li et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2026) focus on editing real-world videos that already possess rich source textures, whereas recent programmable-world evaluation (Huang et al., 2026) primarily examines whether generated videos follow program-logged states and interaction events. Crucially, achieving world preservation does not guarantee faithful visual realization: models frequently retain coarse draft dynamics while failing to generate or temporally bind target appearance, or conversely fulfill appearance prompts at the cost of altering the underlying 4D world. This gap motivates the need for new benchmark that jointly evaluates both objectives to systematically characterize the capability boundaries of generative renderers. In this work, we propose WorldDraft, systematic benchmark designed to evaluate video models as draft-tovideo generative renderers through three progressive questions (Figure 2). First, ➀ can video models render target appearances without corrupting complex 4D worlds? To test this foundational capability, we curate 48 executable 4D world families spanning six challenge categories: multi-entity orchestration, multi-stage dynamics, occlusion and reappearance, camera motion, non-rigid deformation, and hybrid interactions. Grounded in explicit simulator references, WorldDraft jointly measures how faithfully model preserves the prescribed 4D structure and how accurately it realizes and persistently binds target visual attributes over time. Building upon these base worlds, we further probe the capability boundaries of generative renderers along two complementary axes: ➁ how much information must draft provide to support reliable rendering? We then instantiate each world across three draft granularity levels (ranging from abstract proxies to detailed previews) to quantify minimal input requirements and the gains from richer structural and visual cues; and ➂ can models disentangle the world structure to preserve from the source appearance to overwrite? We further pair each draft with three appearance alignment levels (neutral, aligned, and conflicting) under shared target prompt to evaluate selective adherence to structural versus textual conditions. Crossing both axes across all 48 world families yields unified 3 3 factorial design of 432 strictly paired test cases. Through extensive evaluation on WorldDraft, we observe that existing video models struggle to jointly preserve underlying 4D worlds and realize persistent target appearances, especially under coarse draft granularity or conflicting source-target cues (see Figure 1). Motivated by these findings, we further propose WorldDraft-Primer, plug-and-play visual prompting strategy designed to enhance frozen video renderers. Unlike existing adaptation pipelines that rely on costly retraining or privileged simulator access (Li et al., 2026b; Gomez-Nogales et al., 2026), WorldDraft-Primer operates solely on the input draft and target prompt. Specifically, it injects subtle visual cues into the first draft frame via two complementary strategies: (i) object emphasis, which highlights key or easily overlooked entities to reinforce world preservation; and (ii) attribute cueing, which encodes target colors, textures, and shading cues around entities and 2 Figure 2 Overview of WorldDraft. (a) Six challenge categories across 48 executable 4D worlds (shown at P1, AA). (b) 3 3 factorial grid crossing draft granularity (P0 P2) and appearance alignment (AN , AA, AC ). (c) Full benchmark totaling 48 3 3 = 432 cases. supporting surfaces to guide visual realization. Experiments show that WorldDraft-Primer consistently boosts performance across diverse models, serving as both an analytical companion to WorldDraft and practical solution for improving draft-to-video generative rendering. To summarize, this work contributes threefold: We propose WorldDraft, systematic benchmark for draft-to-video generative rendering comprising 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families, organized across six challenge categories and 3 3 factorial grid of draft granularity and appearance alignment levels. Through extensive experiments across 12 representative video models, our findings highlight that: (i) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (ii) finer draft granularity anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (iii) conflicting source cues cause severe source leakage, exposing fragile source-target disentanglement. We further introduce WorldDraft-Primer, simple yet effective plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that injects object emphasis and attribute cues into the first draft frame, consistently boosting both world preservation and visual realization across frozen video renderers.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Code-for-Vision. Emerging works explore executable code as an intermediate representation for 3D reconstruction and scene synthesis (Yin et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026b; Huang et al., 2024a), driving graphics engines to explicitly control geometry, camera parameters, and lighting. Extending this paradigm to dynamic environments, frameworks such as GS-Agent (Zhang et al., 2026) and Code as Worlds (Wang et al., 2026a) describe 4D physical evolution in code, relying on simulators to govern deterministic trajectories and interaction rules. This approach establishes modular division of labor: systems like VideoCoCo (Li et al., 2026b) and Code Video Model (Liang et al., 2026) also employ coding agents to construct simulation drafts, leaving video generation models to synthesize photorealistic outputs. While prior research primarily targets upstream world construction, WorldDraft focuses on the downstream rendering stage, evaluating whether video models can faithfully realize target appearances without corrupting the underlying executable world. Evaluation of Video-to-Video. V2V evaluation has traditionally focused on text-guided editing, measuring instruction adherence, temporal consistency, and background preservation on natural videos (Chen et al., 2025; 3 Li et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2026; Gao et al., 2026). With the rise of programmatic generation, recent benchmarks such as PROWBench (Huang et al., 2026) check behavioral fidelity and event timelines against engine-logged states while evaluating visual quality through holistic metrics such as CLIP. However, such holistic evaluations overlook whether models can faithfully realize fine-grained target attributes and persistently bind them across dynamic 4D processes. In this work, WorldDraft goes step further by investigating how varying input conditions govern the interplay between world preservation and appearance realization.

sections.title: 3.1 Task Formulation
sections.content: Generative Rendering. Programmatic video generation decouples physical reasoning from visual generation: upstream engines explicitly govern scene kinematics, leaving downstream video models to act as renderers. Formally, an upstream simulator executes an underlying 4D world to yield draft video = {Isrc t=1 RT HW 3. Given and target prompt p, generative renderer synthesizes the target video: }T ˆV = G(D, p), (1) where provides the 4D spatiotemporal scaffold (e.g., geometry, kinematics, camera), and dictates target visual attributes (e.g., color, material, lighting). At inference, strictly accesses (D, p), with reserved solely for draft generation and ground-truth evaluation references. Dual Criteria. To determine whether faithfully executes this conditional transformation, the correctness of generative rendering hinges on two criteria: World Preservation, requiring ˆV to faithfully preserve the prescribed 4D kinematics, entity identities, event timelines, and camera motion in without prompt-countermanded structural hallucinations. Visual Realization, requiring ˆV to accurately instantiate target attributes from and persistently bind them to corresponding entities across dynamic motion, occlusions, and viewpoint changes. Generative rendering thus demands that disentangle the world structure to preserve from the source appearance to overwrite: capability fundamentally governed by the drafts input condition.

sections.title: 3.2 Executable World Families
sections.content: Challenge Taxonomy. To evaluate renderers beyond trivial rigid motions, candidate worlds should enforce deterministic physical constraints for world preservation while imposing dynamic stressors for visual realization. Guided by these principles, we first establish 48 executable world families across six primary categories (Figure 2): World Coverage I. Multi-Entity Orchestration: Preserving multi-entity spatial arrangements and coordination, challenging the renderer to bind distinct target attributes without identity cross-contamination. II. Multi-Stage Dynamics: Retaining causal event ordering and phase transitions, challenging attribute persistence across state-changing boundaries. III. Occlusion & Reappearance: Maintaining physical occlusion orders and reappearance trajectories, challenging the renderer to re-identify and restore the exact target appearance post-emergence. IV. Camera Motion: Retaining 6-DoF camera trajectories and parallax geometry, demanding strict multi-view appearance consistency under perspective shifts. V. Non-Rigid Deformation: Retaining continuous mesh topology and soft-body kinematics, requiring surface textures and materials to deform realistically without visual slipping or artifacts. VI. Hybrid Interactions: Retaining dynamic physical coupling across disparate mechanisms (e.g., collisions and force transfer), challenging identity and material retention under violent multi-body contact. 4 Figure 3 Overview of our proposed (Top) WorldDraft benchmark and (Bottom) WorldDraft-Primer strategy. These categories serve as primary stressors rather than disjoint splits; each family is classified by its dominant In particular, multi-entity orchestration focuses on challenge while incorporating secondary dynamics. cooperative spatial topology, whereas hybrid interactions stresses dynamic physical coupling between contact processes. Construction and Validation. For each challenge, we first collect diverse real-world videos as dynamic blueprints, and employ multimodal coding agents (i.e., GPT-6-Astra (Singh et al., 2025)) to translate their underlying physical interactions and camera paths into executable MuJoCo (Todorov et al., 2012) or Blender (Blender Online Community, 2026) scripts. Crucially, the footage serves as world reference rather than target for pixel-level reconstruction. Execution produces deterministic 4D rollouts while programmatically logging the ground-truth state tuple: Wi = (Si, Ti, Ei, Ci), (2) with 3D geometry Si, dense trajectories Ti, event timestamps Ei, and camera poses Ci. Each world passes three-tiered admission audit: ➀ numerical stability without divergence, ➁ fidelity to the reference interaction, and ➂ evaluative viability with unambiguous 4D binding stressors, freezing 48 standardized families, as shown in Figure 3.

sections.title: 3.3 Controlled Draft Design
sections.content: To further isolate whether rendering failures stem from insufficient structural support or deceptive appearance cues, we then freeze the 4D kinematics and prompt pi for each Wi, and further orthogonally vary drafts across two axes: draft granularity and appearance alignment. Prompt Suite. unified prompt pi per family specifies 2 4 verifiable attributes (e.g., color, material, lighting). To guarantee unbiased evaluation, pi enforces: ➀ observable verification via unambiguous visual criteria; ➁ alignment-invariant references that index entities via spatial/semantic roles (e.g., leading cube) rather than volatile appearance tags; and ➂ structural neutrality, strictly omitting trajectories or camera paths so text cannot compensate for draft sparsity. More examples are in Section A. Draft Granularity (P ). To investigate minimal input requirements, we instantiate each world across three monotonic information levels {P0, P1, P2}: ❶ Abstract (P0): Primitive geometries and flat shading; retains basic semantics and kinematics to test low-scaffold completion. 5 ❷ Simulation (P1): Standard physical meshes and basic lighting; serves as the canonical draft-to-video rendering operating point. ❸ Previs (P2): Dense meshes, full context, and realistic shadows; quantifies headroom while retaining synthetic-to-real gap. This axis establishes an information ladder of structural completeness rather than cosmetic image filtering. Appearance Alignment (A). Rich visual cues can either guide rendering or trigger severe source leakage. Therefore, to evaluate adherence to text over deceptive source cues, each granularity is paired with three appearance alignment states {AN , AA, AC}: ❶ Neutral (AN ): Uninformative placeholder shaders (e.g., gray clay), relying solely on text for appearance. ❷ Aligned (AA): Source appearances match pi within the precision of the respective granularity level. ❸ Conflicting (AC): Contradictory source cues (e.g., blue metal vs. target red plastic) to probe source leakage. Variations affect strictly surface appearance without altering geometry Si, kinematics Ti, or camera Ci. Crossing both axes yields unified 3 3 grid of 9 paired inputs D(j,k) for each world, totaling 48 3 3 = 432 strictly paired test cases. Fixing alignment isolates the marginal gain of draft information (01, 12), while fixing granularity isolates conflict sensitivity and source leakage. i

sections.title: 3.4 Evaluation Suite
sections.content: Standard video metrics (e.g., FVD (Unterthiner et al., 2018)) fail to accurately evaluate both world preservation and visual realization directly. We thus establish an analytical suite across three disentangled dimensions: ➀ world preservation (WP), ➁ rendering fidelity (RF), and ➂ appearance persistence (AP). We report these dimensions separately to preserve diagnostic interpretability, with an additional composite score for overall comparison. World Preservation (WP). Grounded in Wi = (Si, Ti, Ei, Ci), WP independently benchmarks: ➀ Entity & Layout (Si), using Count Accuracy and trajectory-matched BBox IoU; ➁ Kinematics & Events (Ti, Ei), via Matched Track Coverage, Interaction Success Rate (ISR), and Event Timing Coverage; and ➂ Camera (Ci), via relative rotation and scale-normalized translation errors against the canonical draft. Metrics evaluate intended topology, ensuring P0 is not penalized for lacking fine details only introduced in P2. Details in Section B.1. Rendering Fidelity (RF). Adherence to pi is evaluated via attribute-level binary QA (Yes/No) across target colors, materials, and lighting, incorporating balanced affirmative/negated probes. Critically, QA judges receive only the target text and generated video, remaining strictly isolated from source drafts to prevent bias. Standard perceptual scores (e.g., Image Quality, Aesthetic) are reported separately as non-gated references VQ. Appearance Persistence (AP). Since maintaining an incorrect appearance over time is not always consistency, we therefore establish correctness-gated persistence metric: AP = QAP qQAP cq sq, (3) where cq {0, 1} verifies target attribute realization at an anchor frame, and sq {0, 1} checks whether the identical entity retains that attribute across subsequent timestamps. Credit is awarded if and only if both pass (cq sq = 1). Grid Diagnostics and Aggregation. On the full 3 3 grid, we designate (P1, AN ) as the canonical operating point and derive two diagnostic quantities: (i) Conflict Penalty, CP = RF(AA) RF(AC), measuring performance drop under conflicting cues, and (ii) Source Leakage, SL = Nsource_leaked/Nconflict, quantifying the erroneous persistence of conflicting source attributes.

sections.title: 4 WorldDraft-Primer
sections.content: The dual correctness criteria of WorldDraft expose an inherent operational dilemma in generative rendering: how to reliably anchor target attributes without corrupting prescribed kinematics. While prompt engineering might seem intuitive, text prompts are inherently spatially agnostic, frequently inducing attribute crosscontamination across multiple entities. Conversely, modifying all draft frames risks destroying the deterministic kinematics and inducing temporal flickering. Leveraging the fact that video diffusion models naturally propagate initial appearances via spatiotemporal attention (Fang et al., 2025; Qi et al., 2026), we propose WorldDraft-Primer, plug-and-play visual prompting strategy. WorldDraft-Primer intervenes strictly on the initial frame Isrc 1 , producing cued frame I1: = (I1, Isrc 2 , . . . , Isrc ), ˆV = G( D, p), (4) leaving the remaining 1 draft frames untouched to preserve the exact physical evolution. sections.content: Models. We benchmark 12 representative video models on WorldDraft, spanning three primary paradigms across 10 open-weight architectures: ➀ Generative Renderers: SolarRenderer-33B (Fang et al., 2026), C2R-14B (Gomez-Nogales et al., 2026); ➁ Omni Models: MiniMax-H3-33B (MiniMax, 2025), LynnReal-Omni-32B (Mao et al., 2026), OmniWeaving-8.3B (Pan et al., 2026), VINO-13B (Chen et al., 2026), UniVideo-13B (Wei et al., 2026); and ➂ Controllable Generators: Bernini-R-14B (Team et al., 2026), Wan2.2-VACE-Fun-A14B (Jiang et al., 2025), Wan2.1-VACE-14B (Jiang et al., 2025). sections.content: LynnReal-Omni and To diagnose why state-of-the-art models struggle with generative rendering, Figure 4 visualizes representative failure cases from top-performing models ( Seedance 2.5) on C05 (Occlusion & Reappearance) and A04 (Multi-Entity Orchestration): Failure Mode ❶: Prompt-driven structural override. When processing dynamic scenes with complex layouts, models frequently sacrifice draft kinematics to satisfy textual semantics. As illustrated in Figure 4 (a), both Seedance 2.5 exhibit near-zero Spatial Preservation (consistently scoring 18.8, dipping to 6.2). Instead of adhering to the prescribed camera trajectory and warehouse shelving geometry, the models synthesize entirely ungrounded viewpoints and forklift trajectories conditioned solely on the prompt. This demonstrates that models easily devolve from faithful renderers into unconstrained text-to-video generators. LynnReal-Omni and Failure Mode ❷: Deficient spatial reasoning and attribute binding. Under neutral scaffolds (AN ), models exhibit weak spatial understanding, failing to parse relative coordinate references and topological arrangements. As shown in Figure 4 (b) , the prompt specifies an ordered 3 4 color layout across 12 sailboats. Lacking the ability to resolve relative spatial hierarchies (e.g., row depths and left-to-right ordering), the models scramble target colors, causing severe attribute cross-contamination. Failure Mode ❸: Previs texture latching and conflicting leakage. Richer drafts and conflicting cues severely disrupt appearance synthesis. sections.title:
5.4 Results with WorldDraft-Primer
Motivated by the failure modes above, we further sought to investigate whether a lightweight test-time
strategy can unlock frozen video renderers without retraining. To this end, we evaluate WorldDraft-Primer
across representative models ( OmniWeaving and MiniMax-H3) against raw baselines and text prompt
engineering (Text PE); results are in Table 2 and Figures 13 and 14.
sections.content: WorldDraft-Primer consistently enhances both world preservation and visual realization. As shown in Table 2, WorldDraft-Primer consistently boosts both world preservation and appearance realization across architectures. For OmniWeaving, WorldDraft-Primer enhances Preservation (+2.99) and Realization (+4.56) while reducing Source Leakage by 3.42%, yielding an Overall gain of +2.51. For MiniMax-H3, it boosts Realization to 80.21 (+3.83) and elevates the Overall score to 65.56 (+1.93), surpassing both Seedance 2.5 (64.73). Conversely, Text PE provides negligible improvements (+0.90 and +1.26), limited by the inherent spatial ambiguity of text. Qualitative results in Figures 13 and 14 further confirm these findings: first-frame cues effectively stabilize global camera framing against unprompted zoom-ins, prevent multi-entity attribute cross-contamination (e.g., binding cobalt-blue exclusively to the rightmost ball in B02), and suppress deceptive source color leakage under AC. sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: In this work, we explored the emerging division of labor between code-driven simulation and video generation by proposing WorldDraft, systematic benchmark of 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families. Extensive evaluations across 12 representative models yield clear answers to our three foundational questions: ➀ world preservation and target appearance realization remain in stark operational tension; ➁ richer draft scaffolding reliably anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and ➂ conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage, exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we introduce WorldDraft-Primer, plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer establish foundational stepping stone toward physically grounded generative rendering.

sections.title: A More Details of WorldDraft
sections.content: A.1 Motivation of Each Challenge Grounded in the dual objectives of world preservation and visual realization, WorldDraft curates dynamic scenarios that jointly impose deterministic physical constraints and multi-modal binding stressors. Evaluating generative renderers on these scenarios probes spatiotemporal reliability across diverse physical regimes: capabilities that conventional static image metrics fundamentally fail to measure. Below, we detail the design motivations behind our six dynamic challenge categories: I. Multi-Entity Orchestration When scenes contain multiple concurrent entities, particularly those with identical geometries, dense clusters, or dynamic spatial swaps, models face severe risks of identity confusion and attribute crosscontamination. This challenge explicitly assesses whether renderer preserves exact instance counts, relative spatial layouts, and coordinated multi-agent trajectories, while accurately binding distinct target attributes (e.g., individualized colors and materials) to their designated semantic roles without spatial bleeding or entity dropping. II. Multi-Stage Dynamics Locally smooth motion does not imply global causal correctness: models often generate visually plausible micro-movements while skipping discrete phase transitions or reversing event sequences. This category evaluates whether key temporal boundaries, causal action-reaction orders, and phase-dependent kinematics are faithfully preserved, while simultaneously requiring target appearances to remain invariant across state-changing boundaries (e.g., mechanical latch unlocking, opening, and locking). III. Occlusion & Reappearance Physical occlusion temporarily removes direct visual evidence of an entity, breaking adjacent-frame continuity and demanding long-range spatiotemporal memory. This challenge measures whether the renderer maintains physical occlusion orders, follows emergence trajectories, and accurately re-identifies the target entity upon reappearance: restoring its precise target color, material, and surface texture rather than resetting or re-synthesizing generic object. IV. Camera Motion Aggressive 6-DoF camera trajectories continuously reshape perspective projections, surface visibility, and parallax depth. This category evaluates whether the model faithfully preserves the canonical camera path and epipolar geometry. It demands strict multi-view appearance consistency, verifying that intrinsic material identities remain stable while view-dependent visual cues (e.g., specular highlights and Fresnel reflections) deform realistically under dynamic perspective shifts. V. Non-Rigid Deformation Unlike rigid bodies with static topologies, soft-body kinematics continuously deform mesh geometries and local surface coordinates. This challenge tests whether continuous topological deformations and structural integrity are preserved, and whether target textures, patterns, and elastic materials conform naturally to the deforming substrate without visual slipping, surface tearing, or texture resetting. VI. Hybrid Interactions Violent physical interactions, such as contact collisions, momentum transfer, and friction, couple the motions of disparate objects into codependent physical systems. Generating plausible individual motions in isolation easily violates joint Newtonian laws. This category focuses on preserving contact boundaries, interaction outcomes, and kinetic energy exchange, while testing whether entity identities and materials 14 Figure 5 Data demonstration of I. Multi-Entity Orchestration. survive intense physical contact. It directly complements Multi-Entity Orchestration by emphasizing dynamic force coupling over static spatial coordination. Each executable world family in WorldDraft is categorized by its primary physical stressor, while naturally incorporating secondary dynamics. Section A.2 illustrates representative cases and paired draft variants. A.2 Data Demonstration Figures 5 to 10 showcase representative cases across all six challenge categories, visualizing the real-world reference footage, target prompt, and the full 3 3 draft grid (P0 P2 AN , AA, AC) for each world.

Therefore, the standalone columns in Table 1 remain essential for diagnosing individual failure modes and capability trade-offs. B.5 Analysis of Metric-Human Alignment To validate the VLM evaluation protocol part of WorldDraft, we compare algorithmic decisions against blind annotations from five independent human judges on randomly sampled test cases, using majority voting as ground truth. As shown in Figure 11, automated metrics achieve strong human agreement across all six dimensions, ranging from 87.5% to 94.2% (averaging 91.0%). Appearance probes exhibit the highest concordance (RF : 94.2%, SL : 92.5%, AP : 91.5%), while physical and count metrics remain highly reliable (ISR : 90.8%, GC : 89.2%, LC : 87.5%). This validates our automated benchmark suite as faithful surrogate for human judgment. Figure 11 Metric-human alignment. Agreement between automated VLM judgments and five-annotator human consensus across sampled cases, averaging 91.0% across all six metrics. More Details of WorldDraft-Primer C.1 Case Demonstration and Analysis Figures 13 and 14 visualize qualitative rollouts across the 3 3 grid for B02 (Newtons Cradle) and D02 (Water-Tank Tower). Across both scenarios, WorldDraft-Primer visibly improves adherence to input drafts: it stabilizes global camera framing against erratic zoom-ins, suppresses ball dropouts in B02 while precisely isolating target colors to the rightmost sphere, and preserves surrounding town layouts in D02 while mitigating deceptive AC roof colors. Capacity Dependency and Method Positioning. Crucially, WorldDraft-Primer operates as lightweight visual prompting strategy whose efficacy remains inherently tethered to the underlying base model. On weaker architectures (e.g., OmniWeaving), the model occasionally struggles to assimilate the injected firstframe cues into photorealistic textures, sometimes faintly echoing prompt brackets across subsequent frames. Furthermore, under dense previs drafts (P2), strong synthetic priors can still bias the renderer toward artificial, plastic-like shading. Ultimately, WorldDraft-Primer serves as an analytical proof-of-concept demonstrating that test-time visual cues can steer frozen video models. Fully overcoming dense prior interference and enabling seamless prompt assimilation remain important challenges for future work. 22 C.2 Ablation Study of WorldDraft-Primer To dissect the individual contributions of Object Emphasis (IOE) and Attribute Cueing (Ient + Ienv), we ablate each component on MiniMax-H3 across the full benchmark. As shown in Figure 12, the two mechanisms exhibit remarkable orthogonality and synergy: Figure 12 Component ablation of WorldDraft-Primer on MiniMax-H3. Removing corner brackets (w/o Object Emphasis) causes sharp collapse across all spatial metrics: Global Count drops from 30.02 to 28.70, Local Count from 45.42 to 43.43, and BBox IoU from 16.70 to 15.97 (falling back near the base model), demonstrating that geometric brackets are indispensable for anchoring coordinates and preventing entity dropouts. Conversely, removing color and environmental hints (w/o Attribute Cueing) cripples appearance metrics, dropping RF from 80.21 to 76.61 and AP from 73.84 to 70.53, while increasing Source Leakage to 26.75%. Crucially, integrating both components achieves the highest score across all six metrics simultaneously, confirming that our design decouples spatial trajectory anchoring from surface attribute binding without mutual interference. C.3 Text Prompt Engineering Baseline (Text PE) Our Text PE baseline adapts Video Prompt Optimization (VPO) (Cheng et al., 2025) for generative rendering under four strict controls: (i) the target prompt is optimized once per world family (pi ) and shared across all nine factorial conditions to preserve paired design; (ii) the meta-prompt enriches descriptive appearance attributes while explicitly delegating kinematics, spatial layout, and camera motion to the draft; (iii) generations use identical random seeds, drafts, and model inference templates; and (iv) all evaluations strictly assess adherence to the original prompt pi, preventing spurious metric shifts. C.4 System Prompt for Visual Prompting To automate first-frame cue generation of WorldDraft-Primer, we deploy Qwen3.5-27B (Yang et al., 2025) as an agentic visual grounding reasoner. Given the target prompt and sampled draft frames, the agent is instructed to: (i) identify and ground key entity boxes in the first frame based on geometry and motion rather than conflicting source colors; (ii) extract target attributes (e.g., specified colors and patterns) from the prompt; and (iii) programmatically invoke cropping and SVG drawing tools to generate minimalist corner brackets and localized attribute cues. The complete system prompt is detailed below: System Prompt for WorldDraft-Primer """ You are visual grounding agent for abstract draft videos . Use ONLY supplied RGB frames and original render prompt . Cuboids and rectangles can represent cars ; do not require photorealistic appearance . Source colors may conflict with desired colors : identify instances by geometry , initial location and motion , not desired color . Never invent objects absent in frame zero . The five INITIAL images come from the SAME video in chronological order : frame 0 , frame 20 , frame 40 , frame 60 , frame 80. They are successive observations , not independent scenes . Associate the same physical object across these frames using its position , shape , spatial relations and observed motion . Determine left - turning versus straight - driving roles from the observed trajectory across frames , not from single - frame arrow , lane position or requested target color alone . Before drawing motion - defined target , include the supporting frame indices and observed movement in its description . If the sampled frames do not establish its identity reliably , omit that target and disclose the uncertainty . After identifying an object across time , return to ORIGINAL frame 0 to locate it . Every output box must use that object frame -0 position ; never substitute later - frame position or add an object absent in frame 0. Subsequent tool - returned crops and drawing previews are inspection views , not additional video time steps ; their order does not indicate motion . The current inspect_crop tool magnifies frame 0 only ; use the five initial images for temporal evidence .

sections.title: D Exhibition Board
sections.content: To provide an exhaustive qualitative autopsy across physical regimes while adhering to submission file size limits, complete high-resolution 3 3 grid rollouts across all six dynamic challenge categories are hosted on our interactive project page: https://haroldchen19.github.io/WorldDraft-site. Below, we analyze Seedance 2.5, representative failure cases from the top-four benchmarked models ( MiniMax-H3, and Wan 3.0). Even among these top performers, models systematically struggle to simultaneously satisfy visual plausibility, 4D structural preservation, and target attribute realization. These qualitative results substantiate three primary insights: LynnReal-Omni, Appearance realism decouples from structural fidelity. Superficial visual quality frequently masks severe structural violations. In C05 (Occlusion & Reappearance), models synthesize photorealistic warehouse textures and forklifts, yet arbitrarily rearrange shelving aisles, alter obstacle depths, and distort occlusion orders. Similarly, in A01 (Multi-Entity Orchestration), MiniMax-H3 introduces unprompted camera rotations away from the canonical top-down view, while Wan 3.0 in F03 transforms dense, orderly domino arrays into sparse irregular blocks. These cases confirm that achieving high visual quality or satisfying isolated appearance QA queries does not equate to faithful generative rendering. Increasing draft granularity does not guarantee Granularity returns are multidimensionally asymmetric. monotonic improvements across all generative axes. While detailed geometry (P2) helps resolve local entity contours, it frequently induces composition drift, under-stylization, or degraded appearance binding. In E03 (Multi-Stage Dynamics), MiniMax-H3 under AN zooms in excessively as granularity increases from P0 to P2, causing the umbrella to drift out of frame. In B05 (Multi-Stage Dynamics), Seedance 2.5 fails to photorealistically stylize dense drafts at P1 and P2, retaining synthetic, toy-like block artifacts despite explicit prompts for painted steel. Higher input granularity thus alters the models visual attention, often trading global framing stability for local geometric detail. Source leakage persists across dense scaffolds. Resolving contradictory appearance cues (AC) requires renderers to simultaneously overwrite misleading pixels while retaining underlying kinematics. However, models consistently treat source colors as uneditable geometry: in C05 at (P1, AC), MiniMax-H3 replicates the deceptive red bodywork of the draft rather than synthesizing the target yellow; in E03 at (P2, AC), Seedance 2.5 faithfully tracks the complex umbrella canopy but tenaciously retains its conflicting red-andwhite stripes, failing to bind target yellow and navy-blue hues. Crucially, even when the draft provides dense, unambiguous geometric scaffolds (P2), models remain vulnerable to source color leakage, underscoring the urgent need for explicit cross-modal disentanglement mechanisms.
